references/step1-legitimate-interest.md.notes: Step 1 of the EDPB three-step test (pursuit of a legitimate interest), per EDPB Guidelines 1/2024. Unchanged since the v1.0 baseline; not touched by the v1.1 citation-audit fixes (CF-14/15/24).

references/step2-necessity.md.notes: Step 2 of the EDPB three-step test (necessity/data minimisation). Unchanged since the v1.0 baseline; not touched by the v1.1 citation-audit fixes.

references/step3-balancing.md.notes: Step 3 of the EDPB three-step test (the balancing test). v1.3 break-it fix (2026-10-02): added an explicit 'Art. 6(1)(f) is never sufficient on its own for Art. 9/10 data' callout under the nature-of-data table, citing GDPR Art. 9(2)(a)-(j) (exhaustive list, verified against gdpr-info.eu: legitimate interest is not one of them, which follows directly from the closed wording of Art. 9(2) itself) and Art. 10 (verified against gdpr-info.eu: criminal-offence processing requires official-authority control or Member State/Union law authorisation with safeguards). C-252/21 Meta v. Bundeskartellamt, EU:C:2023:537 cited as 'see also' with no paragraph pin for the Art. 9(2)-is-exhaustive point (2026-10-02 correction: a paras. 85-90 pin-cite for this point was added without verifying the primary judgment text and was removed — that range could not be confirmed to concern this point rather than the separate Art. 9(2)(e) manifestly-public-data question). The pre-existing para. 89 pin (dataset sensitive in its entirety requires its own Art. 9(2) derogation) on the table row above is untouched and was not part of this correction.
